skill.name: bark-notify
skill.description: Send Bark push notifications when Codex, Claude, or Claude Code finishes a task. The helper includes device, project, status, and summary details.
skill.summary: Send Bark push alerts for completed AI agent tasks.
skill.author: caopulan

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally sends Bark push notifications, so outbound network use and selected environment access are expected. I confirmed real risks around sending task metadata, reading the Bark key, executing the helper command, and dry-run output that can reveal the token. Most high filesystem and path traversal alerts are false positives from documentation placeholders and standard Codex paths.

remediation.issue: Dry-run output can expose the Bark key.
remediation.suggestion: Mask the Bark key when printing dry-run URLs, or print only the destination host.

remediation.issue: Notification payloads can include sensitive task details.
remediation.suggestion: Redact secrets and keep summaries minimal before sending notifications to Bark.

remediation.issue: The documented shell command accepts generated text arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Document safe argument quoting, or provide a wrapper that passes arguments without shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: The helper allows a configurable Bark base URL.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the base URL scheme and document that only trusted Bark endpoints should be used.

content.value_statement: Long-running AI agent tasks can finish while users are away from their terminal. This skill sends concise Bark push notifications with project, status, device, and summary details.
actual_capabilities: Sends Bark push notifications through the day.app API.
Includes device name, project name, status, and summary in the message.
Reads configuration from CODEX_MACHINE_NAME, CODEX_BARK_KEY, and CODEX_BARK_BASE_URL.
Derives a project name from AGENTS.md or the current folder.
Supports an optional project name override on the command line.
Provides a dry-run mode for previewing the notification.
limitations: Requires a valid Bark key before notifications can be sent.
Sends task metadata to an external push notification service.
Does not automatically redact secrets from summaries.
Depends on network access to the configured Bark endpoint.

use_cases.title: Monitor Long Codex Runs
use_cases.description: Receive a phone alert when a long Codex task completes or fails.

use_cases.title: Track Multi-Project Work
use_cases.description: Include project names in notifications so multiple agent sessions are easy to distinguish.

use_cases.title: Report Agent Outcomes
use_cases.description: Send a short status and summary after Claude Code finishes a workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Notify When Finished
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bark-notify when this task is finished. Send status and a short summary without secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Notify With Project Name
prompt_templates.scenario: Repository with a custom project label
prompt_templates.prompt: When the work is complete, send a Bark notification for project {project_name} with the final status.

prompt_templates.title: Notify On Blocked Work
prompt_templates.prompt: If the task is blocked or fails, use bark-notify with status blocked and summarize the next required action.

prompt_templates.title: Notify After Multi-Step Run
prompt_templates.prompt: After all checks finish, classify the result as success, partial, failed, or blocked, then send a concise Bark notification.

output_examples.input: A Codex task finishes tests for the billing service.
output_examples.output: Phone notification titled Billing tests complete with device, project, success status, and a short result summary.

output_examples.input: Claude Code is blocked by missing API credentials.
output_examples.output: Phone notification titled Credential setup blocked with project name, blocked status, and the needed user action.

output_examples.input: A dry-run preview is requested before sending.
output_examples.output: Terminal preview of the notification destination, title, and body instead of sending a push alert.

best_practices: Keep notification summaries short and free of credentials.
Use clear project names so alerts are easy to identify.
Test configuration with dry-run before enabling routine notifications.
anti_patterns: Do not include tokens, keys, or private customer data in summaries.
Do not use untrusted Bark base URLs for normal notifications.
Do not rely on notifications as the only record of task results.

faq.question: What is Bark Notify for?
faq.answer: It sends Bark push notifications when an AI agent task finishes, fails, or becomes blocked.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What configuration is required?
faq.answer: You need CODEX_MACHINE_NAME and CODEX_BARK_KEY. CODEX_BARK_BASE_URL can override the default Bark endpoint.

faq.question: Does it send data outside my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends notification title and body data to the configured Bark endpoint.

faq.question: Can it detect the project name automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It can read AGENTS.md for a project name, or use the current folder name.

faq.question: Should summaries include secrets?
faq.answer: No. Keep summaries minimal and remove credentials, tokens, and private data before sending.
